title: Module Context: 389a as the Canonical Rank-2 BSD Test Case
content: The module establishes curve 389a (y² + y = x³ + x² - 2x, Cremona: 389a1) as the canonical rank-2 BSD verification target, imported from the parent BirchSwinnertonDyer.lean infrastructure. The file documents 7 results: (I) BSD rank consequences; (II) height pairing matrix positive definiteness; (III) numerical bounds on C ≈ 0.7558; (IV) the rank-2 BSD formula axiom; (V) regulator/period structure; (VI) prime conductor 389; (VII) the BSD_Rank2_Verification bundled proof structure. The import `Proofs.BirchSwinnertonDyer` provides EllipticCurveQ, BSD_Weak/BSD_Strong axioms, analyticRank/algebraicRank, LFunction, HeightPairingMatrix2, BSDData. Namespace `BSD389a` localizes all results to this specific curve, allowing future analogues for 433a, 446d, and other rank-2 test cases to coexist.
mathContext: Curve 389a: Weierstrass model $y^2 + y = x^3 + x^2 - 2x$, conductor $N = 389$ (prime), algebraic rank $= 2$, generators $P_1 = (0,0)$, $P_2 = (-1,1)$. BSD data: $\Omega \approx 4.959$, $R \approx 0.1524$, $|\Sha| = 1$, $\prod c_p = 1$, $|\text{tors}| = 1$, giving $C = \Omega R \approx 0.7558$.

title: BSD Forces analyticRank = 2
content: Under the weak BSD conjecture (algebraicRank = analyticRank), combined with curve389a_rank (algebraicRank = 2), we conclude analyticRank = 2. The proof is a simple rewriting: unfold BSD_Weak, rewrite curve389a_rank, take .symm.
mathContext: BSD_Weak E: algebraicRank E = analyticRank E. For 389a: algebraicRank = 2, so BSD gives analyticRank = 2.

title: L(389a, 1) = 0 Unconditionally
content: By Kolyvagin's theorem (BSD_rank_zero_axiom): if L(E,1) ≠ 0 then algebraicRank = 0. For curve 389a with algebraicRank = 2, this is a contradiction. Therefore L(389a, 1) = 0. Note: BSD is not needed — this is an unconditional result from Kolyvagin alone.
mathContext: Kolyvagin (1990): $L(E,1) \neq 0 \Longrightarrow$ algebraicRank$(E) = 0$. Since algebraicRank$(389a) = 2$, we get $L(389a,1) = 0$.

title: Even Analytic Rank and the Kolyvagin Boundary (rank ≥ 2)
content: `curve389a_analyticRank_even_of_BSD` follows immediately from `curve389a_analyticRank_of_BSD`: the witness for `Even 2` is `⟨1, rfl⟩` since `2 = 2 * 1`. `curve389a_rank_beyond_kolyvagin` states algebraicRank ≥ 2 by rewriting with `curve389a_rank : algebraicRank curve389a = 2`. The key significance: Kolyvagin's Euler system method handles rank 0 unconditionally via `BSD_rank_zero_axiom`, and rank 1 via Gross-Zagier + Kolyvagin. For rank ≥ 2, no unconditional theorem connects L-function vanishing order to algebraic rank — making the full BSD formula for 389a inaccessible without additional axioms. The comment 'lies beyond the proven cases' directly reflects this frontier.
mathContext: $\text{Even}\ 2 = \langle 1, \text{rfl} \rangle$ since $2 = 2 \times 1$. Kolyvagin coverage: rank 0 (unconditional via Coates-Wiles/Kolyvagin), rank 1 (Gross-Zagier + Kolyvagin). Rank $\geq 2$: open. For 389a specifically, L''(E,1)/2 = 0.7558... is known numerically (BGZ) but not algebraically.

title: Height Pairing Matrix: Regulator as Determinant and Positive Definiteness
content: The 2×2 height pairing matrix H for generators P₁ = (0,0), P₂ = (-1,1) of curve 389a has entries h₁₁ = ĥ(P₁) ≈ 0.7622, h₁₂ = ⟨P₁,P₂⟩ ≈ -0.1323, h₂₂ = ĥ(P₂) ≈ 0.2720. `curve389a_regulator_is_det` establishes R = h₁₁·h₂₂ - h₁₂² by `rfl` — a definitional equality in HeightPairingMatrix2. `curve389a_height_matrix_pos_def` uses `regulator_pos` from the structure to confirm det H > 0, encoding ℤ-linear independence of P₁ and P₂. `curve389a_height_product_pos` proves h₁₁·h₂₂ > 0 via `mul_pos` applied to h11_pos and h22_pos from the structure's fields.
mathContext: $R = \det(H) = h_{11} h_{22} - h_{12}^2 > 0$ encodes that $P_1, P_2$ generate a rank-2 free abelian group in $E(\mathbb{Q})/\text{tors}$. Values: $R = 7622/10000 \times 2720/10000 - (1323/10000)^2 \approx 0.2073 - 0.0175 = 0.1524 \approx R_{\text{BSD}}$.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz for Height Pairings: Strict Inequality via Non-Orthogonality
content: For any 2×2 height pairing matrix, R = det(H) ≤ h₁₁·h₂₂ with equality iff h₁₂ = 0. For curve 389a, h₁₂ = -1323/10000 ≠ 0, so the inequality is strict: R < ĥ(P₁)·ĥ(P₂). The proof chain: `curve389a_generators_not_orthogonal` establishes h₁₂² > 0 by first rewriting `curve389a_heightMatrix.h12 = -1323/10000` (by `rfl`), then `norm_num`. `curve389a_regulator_strict_cauchy_schwarz` uses `unfold HeightPairingMatrix2.regulator` to expand R = h₁₁h₂₂ - h₁₂², then `linarith [curve389a_generators_not_orthogonal]` to conclude R < h₁₁h₂₂.
mathContext: $\det(H) = h_{11}h_{22} - h_{12}^2 < h_{11}h_{22}$ when $h_{12} \neq 0$. For 389a: $R \approx 0.1524 < 0.7622 \times 0.2720 \approx 0.2073$. The off-diagonal $h_{12} = -1323/10000$ reflects the non-trivial Néron-Tate pairing $\langle P_1, P_2 \rangle$.

title: BSD Constant Numerical Bounds via norm_num
content: The BSD constant C = Ω·R·|Ш|·∏cₚ/|tors|² for curve 389a. With Ω = 4959/1000, R = 1524/10000, |Ш| = 1, ∏cₚ = 1, |tors| = 1: C = 4959 × 1524 / 10⁷ = 7557516/10000000 ≈ 0.7558. All bounds are proved by `unfold BSDData.constant curve389a_BSD; norm_num`, which reduces to rational arithmetic over the exact values in curve389a_BSD. The tighter bounds `curve389a_BSD_constant_approx` prove 7557/10000 < C < 7558/10000, enabling the BGZ consistency check. `curve389a_BSD_constant_eq_omega_times_reg` (proved by `unfold; norm_num`) confirms C = Ω·R since |Ш|, tam, tors = 1.

title: Three Axioms: Strong BSD Formula, L-Derivative Existence, and BGZ Numerical Data
content: Part IV axiomatizes three results that cannot be machine-verified: (1) `BSD_rank2_Lderiv2` — the strong BSD formula for rank-2 curves: L''(E,1)/2 = BSDConstant(E) = Ω·R·|Ш|·∏cₚ/|tors|². This is literally the Millennium Prize conjecture for rank-2 curves. (2) `curve389a_second_L_derivative : ℝ` — a constant declaration introducing the second L-derivative as a real number; this exists in the global namespace but has no definition, formalizing the fact that L''(389a,1) is well-defined (the L-function of 389a analytically continues to order 2 at s=1). (3) `curve389a_BGZ_computation` — the 1985 Buhler-Gross-Zagier numerical bounds: 7557/10000 < L''(389a,1)/2 < 7558/10000, encoding the computational verification. The design principle: axiomatize the deep analytics, formally prove the arithmetic structure around them.
mathContext: Strong BSD rank-2: $L''(E,1)/2! = \Omega \cdot R \cdot |\Sha| \cdot \prod c_p / |\text{tors}|^2$. Axiom (2) is a Lean `axiom` constant (not a theorem), introducing a new real without proof. Axiom (3) encodes the BGZ table: $L''(389a,1)/2 \approx 0.7558$. Combined: BSD predicts $0.7558 \approx C \approx 0.7557516$ — off by $< 10^{-4}$.

title: BGZ Consistency: |L''(389a,1)/2 - C| < 1/1000 via linarith
content: The axiomatized BGZ computation gives 0.7557 < L''(389a,1)/2 < 0.7558. Combined with 7557/10000 < C < 7558/10000, we formally verify |L''(389a,1)/2 - C| < 1/1000. `curve389a_second_L_deriv_pos` follows by `linarith` from the lower BGZ bound. `curve389a_BSD_consistency` uses `rw [abs_lt]`, then splits into two linarith goals: both use the BGZ bounds for L'' and the constant bounds for C. This captures the numerical agreement that Buhler, Gross, and Zagier found in 1985.

title: Part V: Trivial Ш/Torsion/Tamagawa and Regulator Bounds
content: `curve389a_BSD_structure` proves sha = 1, tors = 1, tam = 1 by `rfl` — these are definitional equalities baked into the `curve389a_BSD` structure definition. `curve389a_omega_gt_49` and the regulator bounds (0.15 < R < 0.16, proved by `simp [curve389a_BSD]; norm_num`) pin down the BSD ingredients arithmetically. The `simp [curve389a_BSD]` step unfolds the `BSDData` structure to expose the rational field values, then `norm_num` closes the inequality goal over rationals. `curve389a_reg_bounds` bundles the two one-sided bounds as a conjunction. The key significance: for curve 389a the BSD formula has no Sha or Tamagawa complications (all equal 1), isolating the pure Ω · R product as the BSD constant.
mathContext: For 389a: $|\Sha| = 1$ (trivial Tate-Shafarevich group, consistent with rank 2), $|\text{tors}| = 1$ (no rational torsion: the only torsion over $\mathbb{Q}$ is the identity), $\prod c_p = c_{389} = 1$ (Kodaira type $I_1$ at the unique bad prime). So $C = \Omega \cdot R = 4.959 \times 0.1524$.

title: Prime Conductor 389: Why c₃₈₉ = 1 and the BSD Formula Simplifies
content: Part VI establishes three results about the conductor: primality of 389 (by `norm_num`), the bound 389 > 100 (trivial), and conductor = 389 by `rfl`. The deep significance is arithmetic: a prime conductor means exactly one bad prime, and for curve 389a the reduction type at 389 is multiplicative (Kodaira type I₁, nodal cubic mod 389). The Tamagawa number c₃₈₉ = 1 for Kodaira type I₁, which directly simplifies the BSD formula: ∏cₚ = 1. Primality of 389 can be verified: 389 is not divisible by any prime ≤ √389 < 20 (primes 2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19 do not divide 389).
mathContext: $N = 389$ is prime. Kodaira type $I_1$ at 389 means $c_{389} = 1$. Primality check: $\sqrt{389} < 20$; 389 is odd, not divisible by 3 ($3+8+9=20$), 5 (ends in 9), 7 ($389 = 7 \times 55 + 4$), 11 ($389 = 11 \times 35 + 4$), 13 ($389 = 13 \times 29 + 12$), 17 ($389 = 17 \times 22 + 15$), 19 ($389 = 19 \times 20 + 9$). `Nat.Prime 389` by `norm_num`.
prerequisites: Conductor of elliptic curve over ℚ

title: BSD_Rank2_Verification: A Bundled Proof Witness for Rank-2 Curves
content: `BSD_Rank2_Verification E` is a Lean structure bundling: the BSDData for E, a proof `hcurve` that data.curve = E, a proof `hrank : algebraicRank E = 2`, and a proof `hpos : data.constant > 0`. This separates the data from the arithmetic evidence, following the dependently-typed structure pattern. `curve389a_BSD_verification` is `noncomputable` because BSDData contains `ℝ`-valued fields (real numbers in Lean 4 are noncomputable — classical existence proofs underlie their construction). The noncomputable annotation does not affect logical correctness, only executability. `BSD_rank2_constant_pos` shows that any BSD_Rank2_Verification automatically witnesses positivity, making the structure self-consistent.
mathContext: In Lean 4: `noncomputable` is needed when definitions involve `ℝ`, `ℂ`, or other classically-constructed types. The structure `BSD_Rank2_Verification E` is a dependent record: `hcurve : data.curve = E` is a propositional equality, `hrank : algebraicRank E = 2` depends on the specific curve. `curve389a_BSD_verification.data.constant = 7557516/10000000` (exact rational). `BSD_rank2_constant_pos v := v.hpos` is a projection.
